Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sarvesh Pandey Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.
1.
Heard Mr. Ashok Kumar Maurya, the learned counsel for revisionist, the learned A.G.A. for State and Mr. Sarvesh Pandey, the learned counsel representing opposite party-2.

2. Challenge in this criminal revision is to the order dated 28.08.2023 passed by Special Judge,
(POCSO Act)/ Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 8, Ballia in Sessions Trial No. 603 of 2023 arising out of case Crime No. 91 of 2023 under Section 376 I.P.C., 5L/6, 12/14 of POCSO Act and 67-B of I. T. Act, Police Station, Dokati, District-Ballia whereby the application dated 09.08.2023 filed by accused/revisionist under Section 311 Cr.P.. (Paper No. 14 Kha) has been rejected.
3.

entities.text:
Special Judge,
(POCSO Act)/ Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 8, Ballia
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for revisionist contends that order impugned dated 28.08.2023 passed by court below is unsustainable in law and fact.

It is an admitted fact that revisionist is an accused in above Vikas Pasi vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142464011/
1 mentioned sessions case.

entities.text: above Vikas Pasi vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the right of an accused/revisionist to cross-examine the prosecutrix was closed.

Accordingly, accused/revisionist filed an application dated 09.08.2023 (
Paper No. 14 Kha) in terms of Section 311 Cr.P.C. seeking recall of the prosecutrix so that she could be further cross-examined by/on behalf of accused-revisionist.

In the interest of justice, court below ought to have allowed the said application inasmuch as no prejudice could have been caused either to the prosecutix or the defence in case the prosecutrix was further cross-examined.
He further submits that justice should only be done but also seem to be done .
On the above premise, he contends that order impugned is liable to be set aside by this Court, and the application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. filed by accused-revisionist is liable to be allowed.
4. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. for State-opposite party-1 and the learned counsel representing opposite party-2 have vehemently opposed the present criminal revision.
They submit that in view of the recital contained in the order impugned it is evident that sufficient opportunity was granted to the revisionist to cross-examine the prosecutrix.
Twice the revisionist deliberately changed his counsel.
The order impugned further records that partial cross-examination of the prosecutrix was got done on behalf of the revisionist which runs into four pages.
The said cross-examine was conducted by new counsel engaged by revisionist.
Thereafter, revisionist against changed his counsel and engaged another counsel.
However subsequent counsel filed an application for adjournment/stay of proceedings for the day and thereafter did not appear on behalf of the revisionist to cross-examine the prosecutrix.
Court below considering the provisions of Section 33 and 35 of the POCSO Act, rejected the adjournment/stay application and further closed the cross-examination of prosecutrix.
5. On the above premise, the learned A.G.A. contends that no illegality has been committed by court below in passing the order impugned.
He therefore contends that in view of above no good ground exits to entertain the present criminal revision.

6. The learned counsel representing opposite party-2 has adopted the arguments raised by the learned A.G.A.
7.
When confronted with above, the learned counsel for revisionist could not overcome the same.

8. Having heard the learned counsel for revisionist, the learned A.G.A. for State, the learned counsel representing opposite party-2, upon perusal of record and coupled with the fact that objections raised by the learned A.G.A. in opposition to the present criminal revision could not be dislodged by the learned counsel for revisionist therefore this court does not find any good ground to entertain the present criminal revision.
Revisionist has been playing hide and seek with court below.

As such,
he cannot he allowed to have the benefit of his own wrong.

Moreover, upon perusal of the order impugned this Court finds that court below has neither committed a jurisdictional error in passing the order impugned nor has it exercised it's jurisdiction with material irregularity warranting interference by this Court.
9. In view of the discussion made above, present criminal revision fails and is liable to be dismissed.
